sections.content: Irving, Texas does not always grab headlines the way Dallas or Fort Worth do, but experienced investors know better. Tucked right between those two major cities, Irving offers a rare combination of affordability, strong rental demand, and a consistent pipeline of distressed properties. Whether you are wholesaling your first contract or building a long-term rental portfolio, the real estate deals in Irving TX deserve your attention. If you are just getting started, check out our [Real Estate Investing for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) guide before diving in — it lays the groundwork you will need to succeed in any market.
Irving TX Market Overview: Why Investors Are Paying Attention

Irving sits in Dallas County and covers about 67 square miles. The city is home to roughly 240,000 residents and serves as the headquarters for major companies including Kimberly-Clark, Celanese, and several others along the Las Colinas Urban Center corridor. That corporate base keeps the local economy stable and drives consistent housing demand. The area also benefits from Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport being just minutes away, making it attractive to business travelers, corporate relocators, and short-term rental operators alike. Irving is not a boom-and-bust market — it is a slow-and-steady performer that rewards patient, data-driven investors.
Average Home Prices and What the Numbers Tell You

As of late 2024, the median home price in Irving hovers around $310,000, down slightly from the peak of roughly $340,000 seen in 2022. That softening has created real opportunity. Distressed and off-market properties are frequently available in the $180,000 to $240,000 range, while fully renovated homes in desirable neighborhoods can sell for $380,000 to $450,000. That spread is what makes flipping and wholesaling viable here. Average days on market for move-in-ready homes is around 28 to 35 days, which signals healthy buyer demand without the frenzied competition of 2021. Rent rates for single-family homes typically run between $1,600 and $2,400 per month depending on size and neighborhood, giving buy-and-hold investors solid cash flow potential.

Plug in the address, square footage, and condition to get an instant after-repair value estimate so you know your maximum allowable offer before you pick up the phone.
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investors in Irving
Valley Ranch

Valley Ranch is one of Irving's most recognizable master-planned communities. Homes here were largely built in the 1980s and 1990s, which means a steady supply of properties that need cosmetic updates. Investors who can modernize kitchens and bathrooms see strong resale demand from young families and corporate transplants. The neighborhood's canal system and mature trees make it visually appealing, which helps move renovated properties quickly.
West Irving and Senter Park

West Irving offers some of the most affordable entry points in the city. You will find older homes from the 1950s through 1970s in this area, many owned by long-term residents who are now aging in place or considering a sale. This is fertile ground for wholesalers who know how to build relationships with motivated sellers. Senter Park nearby has seen gradual gentrification pressure from the growing Las Colinas employment corridor, which is pushing values up steadily.
Las Colinas

Las Colinas skews toward higher price points and condo conversions, but investors focused on furnished short-term rentals or corporate housing will find strong demand here. Proximity to major employers and the DFW airport makes this area ideal for mid-term rental strategies targeting traveling professionals.
Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Irving TX

items: Wholesale Deals: West Irving and older residential pockets near Highway 183 consistently produce motivated sellers. Look for probate leads, tax-delinquent properties, and absentee owners — classic wholesale deal sources. You can explore deal structure basics in our [Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners) guide.

Fix and Flip: Valley Ranch and North Irving offer the best flip margins. A typical scenario might involve buying a 3-bed, 2-bath home for $215,000, investing $45,000 in renovations, and reselling for $335,000 — yielding a gross profit near $75,000 before holding costs and closing fees.

Buy and Hold Rentals: With average rents between $1,600 and $2,400 and relatively affordable purchase prices compared to Dallas proper, cash-on-cash returns of 6% to 9% are achievable in Irving when you buy right.

Short-Term and Mid-Term Rentals: Las Colinas and areas near the Toyota Music Factory see strong demand for furnished short-term stays. Corporate housing near DFW airport is another angle worth exploring.

BRRRR Strategy: Irving's market supports the Buy, Rehab, Rent, Refinance, Repeat model well. Properties in West Irving and Senter Park are often undervalued enough to support a full capital pull after refinancing at post-renovation appraised values.

sections.content: Local Market Trends Shaping Irving Real Estate in 2024

Several trends are reshaping the Irving investment landscape right now. First, interest rate pressure has slowed retail buyer activity, which means more motivated sellers and less competition at the negotiating table. Second, institutional investors who flooded the DFW market in 2021 and 2022 have pulled back, leaving more inventory for individual investors. Third, the ongoing corporate expansion in Las Colinas is driving infrastructure investment across the city, which historically lifts surrounding residential values over a 3 to 5 year horizon. Finally, Dallas County's population continues to grow, adding roughly 100,000 new residents per year to the broader metro area — a tailwind for rental demand that benefits Irving landlords directly.

The best real estate markets are not always the flashiest ones. Irving is a textbook example of a workforce housing market with strong fundamentals — steady jobs, growing population, and enough aging housing stock to keep deal flow alive for years.
How to Find Off-Market Deals in Irving

The most profitable real estate deals in Irving TX rarely hit the MLS. To compete, you need to build a pipeline of off-market opportunities. Direct mail campaigns targeting absentee owners and tax-delinquent properties in zip codes 75061, 75062, and 75038 are a reliable starting point. Driving for dollars in West Irving and older neighborhoods near Pioneer Park can surface distressed properties before they ever get listed. Probate court records at the Dallas County courthouse are publicly available and often overlooked by newer investors. For a deeper playbook on sourcing properties before they hit the open market, read our guide on [How to Find Off-Market Real Estate Deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/off-market-real-estate-deals).
Tips for Out-of-State Investors Targeting Irving

Irving is one of the more accessible Texas markets for remote investors because of its strong local infrastructure, reliable property management options, and predictable rental demand. That said, investing from a distance requires extra diligence. Before committing to a deal, make sure you have vetted comps, a reliable local contractor, and a property manager you trust. Texas is a non-disclosure state, which means sale prices are not always public — this makes building relationships with local agents and wholesalers especially valuable. Always run your numbers conservatively and account for Texas property taxes, which can run 2.0% to 2.5% of assessed value annually.

items: Partner with a local investor-friendly real estate agent who specializes in distressed properties and understands ARV in each Irving submarket.
Get repair estimates from at least two local contractors before closing — rehab costs in DFW have risen 15% to 20% since 2020.
Use a title company experienced with wholesale assignments and simultaneous closings if you plan to wholesale deals remotely.
Join the Greater Dallas Real Estate Investors Association (REIA) to connect with local wholesalers, hard money lenders, and property managers.
Analyze every deal with a clear exit strategy — know whether you are wholesaling, flipping, or holding before you make an offer.
Use our free [Wholesale Deal Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/wholesale-deal-calculator) to quickly determine your maximum allowable offer and potential assignment fee on any Irving deal.

sections.content: When analyzing Irving flip deals, target properties at or below 70% of ARV minus repairs. For rental acquisitions, run your numbers at 95% occupancy with a 10% property management fee built in. Conservative underwriting protects you when the unexpected happens — and it always does.
